title: Provisional measurement review
notice: These are newly derived, unvalidated educational observations. The source supplies no printed answer key for this exercise. They are unscored and require qualified ECG educator review.

fields.basis: Visually checked ventricular peaks and measured R–R intervals in original PDF 502
fields.reason: R–R intervals: 0.829 s, 0.805 s, 0.813 s, 0.789 s, 0.821 s, 0.805 s, 0.837 s. These describe the short displayed sample, not an independently adjudicated rhythm diagnosis.

fields.reason: Mean R–R estimate 73.7 bpm; six-second count estimate 80 bpm. These methods differ with phase at the strip endpoints, especially for irregular rhythms. The strip itself has no printed paper-speed label.

fields.value: Candidate P-wave observation: Rounded upright pre-QRS deflections recur before eight small biphasic ventricular complexes. Long intervening nearly level segment makes isolated atrial candidates plausible; no origin diagnosis is established.

fields.value: Approximately regular ventricular spacing over this short strip, with a conditional mean rate near 74 bpm and recurring separate P-like lobes. Sinus origin requires confirmation of uniform sinus P waves and a consistent 1:1 P-QRS relationship. The conditional PR range crosses 0.12 s and QRS range crosses 0.12 s, so the course normal-sinus interval pattern is not established.
fields.basis: New unvalidated educational synthesis of the original raster, accepted conditional measurements and course criteria; not a source-authored rhythm answer
fields.reason: Any named rhythm is a conditional teaching hypothesis, not an assigned diagnosis or scored answer. Rate and duration estimates assume course speed of 25 mm/s, not a verified strip speed. Candidate P identity, atrial origin and conduction remain unadjudicated. Qualified ECG educator review has not occurred.

limitations: New wave-field estimates remain provisional and unscored. Range width reflects uncertain endpoints and reader disagreement, not a validated diagnostic category. QT/QTc, calibrated amplitudes and clinical diagnosis are not established.
The exact original PDF was checked. The inspected waveforms are embedded rasters; larger rendering does not add samples. Expert interpretation may still improve unresolved component identification.
Calibration assumes the course’s 25 mm/s convention (PDF pages 228, 230, 231 and 234). Every image grid was checked separately; the assumption is not a per-strip speed label.
Peak positions are approximate to about ±2 source pixels; morphology, low-amplitude P waves and boundaries remain uncertain. This is not a statistical confidence interval.
